data.name: Description
data.value: One agent per kind of task: its name, what it is given, its instructions and the tools the model sees while it answers. The Jarvis agent receives every request, answers the simplest ones and hands the others over. An agent gives no right: every tool call still goes through the permissions. Each agent is a text file you can edit; Jarvis never replaces a file you changed.

data.name: NoTools
data.value: No tool is on: Jarvis does not hand over to it.

data.name: ToolsOff
data.value: Named in the file, but off or missing: {0}

data.name: OpenFailed
data.value: The file could not be opened. It is in the folder shown above.

data.name: BuiltIn
data.value: Its file is missing or does not read: Jarvis uses the agent that ships with the application.

data.name: Problem_Unreadable
data.value: {0}.md: the file could not be read.

data.name: Problem_NoHeader
data.value: {0}.md: the header is missing. The file must start with a "---" line, then name, description and tools, then another "---" line.

data.name: Problem_NoDescription
data.value: {0}.md: the header has no "description:" line. Without it, Jarvis does not know what to give this agent.

data.name: Problem_NameTaken
data.value: {0}.md: another file already gives this name to an agent.
